newsitem.title: BRAZIL: AIDS spreading fast among Brazilian women - study.
newsitem.headline: AIDS spreading fast among Brazilian women - study.

text.p: AIDS is spreading at an alarming rate among women in Brazil, where the number of women carrying the HIV virus will equal that of men by the year 2000, according to a study published on Saturday.

The United Nations study, which was published in Brazilian newspapers, said an increase in intravenous drug use since the mid-1980s and higher rates of HIV infection among heterosexuals were the main causes for the rise in the number of HIV cases in women.
Currently, the ratio of HIV-infected women to men is one to three in Brazil, compared to just one in 40 when officials began keeping statistics in 1983, the study said.
If that pace is kept up, the ratio will hit one to one by the year 2000, it said. Women now account for about 40 percent of all new AIDS cases worldwide, the study said.

Brazil has one of the world's highest rates of HIV infection, with some 95,000 cases officially registered. Health officials, however, estimate that as many as 450,000 Brazilians might actually be carrying the HIV virus, out of a total population of 160 million.
Some 51 percent of Brazil's HIV carriers live in the state of Sao Paulo, with 14 percent in Rio de Janeiro, the study said.
